title: Tenant-triggered sensitivity eval harness and privacy guardrails for Dedicated/Private
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Build a per-tenant, triggerable evaluation harness that runs targeted quality and sensitivity checks whenever a model version, runtime config (quantization, batching, kernel profile), or routing policy changes for Dedicated and Private customers. The harness must preserve customer data isolation and offer two execution modes: (1) in-customer VPC/on-prem runner (preferred for high-sensitivity tenants) and (2) Redwood-hosted sandboxed runner that uses anonymized or synthetic goldensets.

Why: Customers on Dedicated/Private deployments require assurance that configuration or model changes do not cause regressions for their critical prompts or compliance-sensitive workflows. Central eval infra today runs global suites that cannot safely or practically run on customer corpora. We need a lightweight, tenant-scoped system that can be invoked automatically on change events and produce actionable regression signals without exposing sensitive data.

Goals:
- Trigger per-tenant evals for: model version changes, quantization profile changes, kernel/runtime upgrades, routing policy updates, and major batching/cache tuning.
- Surface a small set of explainable metrics (sensitivity delta, accuracy/regression score, hallucination rate, latency P95 delta) and a binary pass/fail summary per tenant.
- Ensure data never leaves customer-controlled boundaries for Private/Dedicated customers who opt into in-VPC execution. For hosted sandbox runs, enforce anonymization and synthetic reference generation.
- Provide configurable alert thresholds and automated rollback/fallback policies integrated with console rollouts.

Key user stories: 
- As an enterprise ML engineer, I want my tenant’s golden prompts to be evaluated on every runtime change in our VPC so I can sign off on rollouts without exporting data.
- As a platform owner, I want a single UI and API to compare pre/post metrics and trigger canaries or automatic fallback based on tenant rules.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not include full UI polished experiences for long-term audit reporting (follow-up ticket). It focuses on the eval plumbing, privacy modes, metric definitions, and automated gating hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant eval trigger fires for model/config change events and creates a run record with pre/post metrics within 30s of event
Support for two execution modes: in-VPC runner (Docker/K8s image + lightweight orchestrator) and Redwood-hosted sandbox with anonymized goldens
Eval output schema includes: sensitivity_delta, quality_score_delta, hallucination_rate_change, latency_p95_change, and pass/fail tag
No customer prompt/plaintext leaves customer VPC in in-VPC mode; verification tooling + automated attestations are present
Configurable alerting rules available via Console for customer and Redwood SRE teams
Integration with rollout policies: can block a model rollout or automatically shift to fallback variant when tenant-level fail condition met
design_decisions: Use a small standard SDK that customers can import to run local evals; SDK will call local runner that pulls approved model artifacts from customer-signed storage paths
Golden sets: provide two options: customer-managed golden set (preferred) and Redwood-synthesized golden set template when customers cannot upload private corpora
Metric computation occurs inside the runner; only aggregated metrics and cryptographic attestations are returned to Redwood control plane
For hosted sandbox runs, run the evals on synthetic copies derived by reversible-hashing and token-level obfuscation where necessary
Keep eval runs bounded in compute by default (e.g., 200 prompts, 3 generations each) to limit cost and latency
runbook_notes: If a tenant’s sensitivity_delta > threshold, mark rollout as BLOCKED and notify SRE and customer contacts
For transient infra failures during in-VPC runs, retry up to 2 times before marking as INCONCLUSIVE
Logs: store only metadata and cryptographic proof of run; raw prompt outputs must be retained only per tenant policy and not shipped to Redwood S3 for Private deployments
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers may misconfigure VPC runner causing data exfil. Mitigation: deliver hardened runner images, attestation proofs, and a guided onboarding checklist.

Risk: Synthetic goldens might not catch tenant-specific regressions. Mitigation: allow customers to upload private goldens into a customer-managed bucket (encrypted) and strongly encourage for high-risk tenants.
Risk: Added latency to rollout pipelines. Mitigation: make per-tenant evals asynchronous with explicit SLA (e.g., 10-minute window) and provide an opt-in fast-path for blocking canaries
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Implement eval runner spec, metric definitions, and event triggers (server-side hooks). Deliver in-VPC runner PoC and hosted sandbox prototype.
Phase 2: Add attestation layer, Console integration for per-tenant thresholds and UI for run comparisons, and automatic rollback hooks for rollouts.
Phase 3: Harden runner images, SOC/security review, and full rollout to Dedicated customers with onboarding docs and templates
